title: The Last Spire Again
premise: Odile Blackwood, once a battle-sworn mercenary of the silent god Vess, hides in the magic-outlawed city of Corvane selling harmless charms—until a mute child arrives speaking Old Tongue, the language of a kingdom that was erased from history. The child is a living key to the Last Spire, the door through which Odile's god and homeland were sealed away, and hunters from the Church of the Unwritten are closing in. Pursued across a country that officially never existed, Odile must choose between reopening the Spire to restore their god and people, or sealing it forever to save the child's life, which the door demands as payment. In the end, Odile refuses both bargains: they give up their own sworn bond—the last thread connecting them to Vess—to walk the child home, choosing belonging in the present over resurrection of the past.
about_author: Felix Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing extinct languages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people outliving their own histories, and live quietly near a coastline that appears on no old maps.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A day in Corvane: selling luck-knots, dodging Church inspectors, hiding the faint warmth of old vows under their skin. Establishes loneliness and the law against magic. Emotional beat: weary self-erasure; Odile has made invisibility an art.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During a storm, a mud-caked child appears at Odile's threshold speaking a language Odile hasn't heard since the fall—and understands without trying. The child carries a shard of black glass shaped like a spire. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant recognition; the past has found them.

chapters.title: What the Law Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A Church censor, Magistrate Halloway, canvasses the street after reports of 'unlicensed speech.' Odile lies well but notices the child's words leave frost on windows. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; hiding a person is harder than hiding a past.

chapters.title: Old Tongue, Older Debt
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with flashback. Memories of swearing service to Vess at the Spire, the god's final silence three years ago, and the oath-mark that still aches. The child's name, spoken only in Old Tongue, is Sef. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing; duty never really ended.

chapters.title: The Unwritten
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, fragmentary and dreamlike. The child flees a memory of white-robed hunters who erase names as they walk. Sef remembers being chosen, not born. Emotional beat: terror rendered innocent; the reader learns the stakes through a child's eyes.

chapters.title: A Buyer in Ash Street
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. An old comrade, Bren the cartographer, recognizes the spire-shard and offers passage out of the city—for a price Odile can't pay in coin. First hint that others survived the fall. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as a transaction.

chapters.title: Frost on Every Window
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Halloway raids the district; Odile escapes with Sef through the charm-sellers' tunnels, leaving behind the shop and the life built there. Emotional beat: severance; survival means burning what you've grown.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Odile and Bren's POV alternating. They travel a road that maps refuse to show, toward the borderlands of the erased kingdom. Sef grows stronger the closer they get; the shard warms. Emotional beat: uneasy momentum; going home by going somewhere that doesn't exist.

chapters.title: Village of Second Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A hidden village of survivors who took new names to live—they beg Odile not to reopen the Spire, having paid its price before. Introduces Maren, a survivor healer who knew Odile's sworn-brother. Emotional beat: belonging offered with conditions; love begins here.

chapters.title: Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile and Maren's POV. Maren tends Odile's failing oath-mark and tells the truth: the Spire opens only for a life freely given. She asks Odile to stay instead—to belong among the living. Emotional beat: tenderness against duty; the first real temptation to stop running.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Ford
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Unwritten catch them at the river crossing; Bren dies holding the ford, buying hours with a cartographer's last trick—a false map burned into his own skin. Emotional beat: cost made flesh; every mile has a body price.

chapters.title: What Sef Remembers
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The child reveals they were made from the Spire itself—a vessel meant to be given back so the door will open. Sef doesn't want to be a key. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the innocent knows exactly what everyone is deciding about them.

chapters.title: The Silent Answer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At a ruined shrine, Odile prays to Vess for the first time in three years—and receives silence, then something worse: the oath-mark answering in Sef's voice. The god isn't dead; it's waiting inside the child. Emotional beat: vertigo; faith curdles into horror.

chapters.title: Council of the Erased
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Survivors, smugglers, and Maren debate: open the Spire with Sef, destroy it and lose everything forever, or run. Odile argues for a third path no one believes exists. Emotional beat: fracture; allies become factions.

chapters.title: Halloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Odile and Halloway's POV. The magistrate corners them—not with chains but with a deal: surrender the child and the Church will let the hidden villages stand. He reveals he too lost someone to the erasure. Emotional beat: the enemy humanized; the trap is sympathy.

chapters.title: Night of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Someone sells their route to the Church to save the village. Maren covers the betrayal, then confesses to Odile and asks forgiveness she won't grant herself. Emotional beat: love tested by loyalty; forgiveness as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: Odile and Sef's POV. They climb to the Last Spire through the Unwritten's cordon, guided by Bren's false map turned true. The country around them flickers between existing and not. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; Odile finally knows what they're willing to lose.

chapters.title: The Door Demands
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the Spire's threshold, Vess speaks at last—through Sef—demanding the payment promised. Odile refuses to give the child and refuses to abandon the god, offering instead their own oath, their bond, their place in Vess's memory. Emotional beat: defiance; the climax of love against duty.

chapters.title: Unsworn
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, interior and raw. The god accepts: the oath burns out of Odile, and with it every memory of the old kingdom begins to fade. Sef, freed from being a key, becomes simply a child. Emotional beat: sacrifice completed; becoming no one to let someone else become someone.

chapters.title: The Spire Closes
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The door seals with Vess's silence now chosen rather than imposed. The erased country settles into true rest. Sef takes Odile's hand as the memories drain away—except one: Sef's name, which Odile taught the world to keep. Emotional beat: release; grief and grace in the same breath.

chapters.title: A City That Lets You Stay
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Months later: no powers, no god, patchy memory, a small stall again—but this time shared with Sef, with Maren visiting, with neighbors who know their face. Halloway looks the other way, owing his own quiet debt. Emotional beat: earned peace; belonging chosen over destiny.

chapters.title: The Name That Remained
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, closing. On the anniversary, Odile finds a frost-pattern on the window spelling Sef's name in Old Tongue—whether Vess's farewell or just winter, they'll never know. Odile teaches the name to the village children so it outlives them all. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; survival was worth its price because someone carried it forward.
